long_biography.plain_text:
Lebda was born in Lewisburg, Pennsylvania, and studied business administration at Bucknell University before working as an auditor and consultant. Frustration while seeking a first mortgage persuaded him that borrowers needed an easier way to compare lenders, prompting him to establish LendingTree in 1996.

He developed LendingTree as a digital marketplace in which financial providers compete for consumers. Lebda guided the company through its public listing, acquisition by IAC, and subsequent spin-off, returning as chairman and chief executive and remaining in those roles until his death in 2025. Alongside his wife, Megan, he created a family foundation supporting upward mobility, financial wellness, entrepreneurship and rural health care.
